threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus driver asks for exact change; everyone else just pulls out cash without a second thought.
Last night on the 59, I overheard a couple arguing about an ex they hadn’t seen in years. So detailed, it felt like watching a soap opera unfold.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in a tutu juggling flaming torches outside the Kiosk on Hermannplatz at 2 AM. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You know you're in Kreuzberg when late-night kebab shops play 90s Turkish pop, and it's as normal as a beer garden on a sunny day.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know to skip BART on Friday evenings—nothing like overheated brakes and a smoke scare to ruin plans.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni driver busting out an impromptu dance between stops. The passengers loved it—guess the delays bring out the life!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just hop on any tram, but those of us living here know the 3 is a rare sight after 10 PM. Missing it means a long walk or more waiting.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re still clutching that oversized map while trying to navigate the metro. You can spot them pausing at every corner, looking befuddled.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You believe a ‘local’ café can be found just around the corner but end up at a hipster brunch spot with a 45-minute wait.
Last night on the 196, a guy serenaded everyone with an out-of-tune version of 'Wonderwall' while debating the best chicken shops in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of kids using a street vendor's table as a makeshift stage for pop-up performances, I realized I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a late-night döner kebab stand selling currywurst at 3 AM, all while a punk band plays on the street corner.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their reaction to BART delays; they just roll their eyes and check their phone, while newcomers look panicked.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo hopping on the 31. He even adjusted his bow tie before sitting down. Muni’s the real red carpet around here.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about parks and plazas, but the real charm is in the narrow streets with quirky shops that stay open late.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they struggle to order a coffee without saying 'café con leche'—locals know it's just 'café'.
